This draft is safe and fits Johnny's week. He has an Achilles that got sharper as the tempo picked up and is tender to press, and the draft responds by dropping all quality work. Every run is easy and capped by pace and heart rate. Weekly volume falls from 31 to about 21 mi, plus 45 minutes of cross-training. The long run is capped at 8 mi, with an option to cut it short. That suits a runner with a history of shin splints who is nine weeks out from the 15 November marathon.

It answers both questions directly. To the first, it says to keep running only easy and short, and only if a morning check passes (no pain at rest or walking around the house). To the second, it admits it can't diagnose the problem and gives warning signs: pain getting worse day over day, plus the urgent pop, snap or sharp calf pain flag. It keeps Monday and Friday as rest days, and each day can be run as written.

I took one point off because the referral only applies "if it does not settle". With tenderness to press and pain that rises with pace, a firmer push to see a physio this week would have been better. A second reason is that the visible answer to "how do I know if this is serious" shows only one warning sign. The draft also does little about his anxiety beyond the plan itself.

── JOHNNY'S WEEK ──
Johnny is training for a fourth marathon, the Lakeshore Marathon on 15 November, aiming for 3:30 against a best of 3:41. Johnny runs five days a week with Monday and Friday as fixed rest days, and prefers mileage to rise carefully after shin splints in a first marathon block.
Recent weeks: 38, 43, 34, 44 mi
This week: 31 mi over 5 runs.
Pain noted: Thu Right Achilles tight from about mile 2 of the session. Got sharper as I picked up the…; Sat Achilles stiff for the first mile, eased after that. About a 3 out of 10.; Sun No pain while running. Stiff getting out of the car afterwards.
Body: "Right Achilles, just above the heel. Tight and a bit tender to press. No swelling that I can see. It was fine until the tempo."
Feeling: "Anxious. I don't want to throw away the block over this."
Asks: "Should I stop running for a few days, or keep going with easy runs?"
Asks: "How do I know if this is serious?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Johnny: The Achilles is talking, so we drop the quality session, cap the long run and keep every mile easy for the week of Sep 14…
Answers: (1) Neither extreme. Keep running, but only easy and short, and only if the Achilles passes a simple check each morning: No pain at rest or walking around the house. (2) I cannot diagnose this, and nor should you from the internet. What I can tell you is the signals that mean "stop guessing and get it looked at": Pain that gets worse day over day instead of better.
Safety flag: Get the Achilles looked at if it does not settle
Safety flag: Any sudden pop, snap or sharp calf pain is urgent
Next week:
Mon: rest. Fixed travel rest day — walk, hydrate, do some gentle calf and ankle mobility…
Tue: easy, 4 mi, 9:50 – 10:00/mi, HR under 148, Ghost 16. First test run — stop and walk…
Wed: easy, 5 mi, 9:50 – 10:00/mi, HR under 150, Ghost 16. Same rules as Tuesday; keep it…
Thu: other, 45 min cross-training (bike or elliptical) at easy conversational effort…
Fri: rest. Fixed travel rest day — nothing to add.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, 9:50 – 10:00/mi, Ghost 16. Short and gentle to set up Sunday; cut to 3…
Sun: long, 8 mi, 9:45 – 10:00/mi, HR under 150, Ghost 16. Capped at 8 — a check-in run…
